title: Protocol to test the utility of detergents for E. coli membrane protein extraction and delipidation
protocol: Filter solvents through a syringe filter prior to the experiment.
Clean and prepare stock solutions for detergents before starting the experiment.
Prepare a dilution series of hybrid detergent in filtered MilliQ water with concentrations between 10^-8 and 10^-2 mol/L.
Make stock solution A and filter it through a syringe filter.
Prepare stock solution B from stock solution A.
Proceed to prepare stock solutions C-F accordingly for accurate concentrations.
Rinse a Quartz Suprasil Semi-micro cuvette (2 mm x 10 mm) with filtered methanol (3 times, 1 mL each).
Rinse the same cuvette with filtered MilliQ water (3 times, 1 mL each).
Turn on the Zetasizer Nano-ZS and allow it to warm up for 30 minutes.
Set the instrument parameters as required for DLS measurement.
Use a glass Pasteur pipette to wash the cuvette with approximately 0.5 mL of the lowest concentration of detergent stock (0.0001 mg/mL).
Discard the detergent solution.
Load approximately 0.5 mL of the same detergent concentration (0.0001 mg/mL) into the cuvette using a new Pasteur pipette.
Place the cuvette into the sample holder of the Zetasizer instrument.
Start the measurement following the parameters defined in the software.
Thermally equilibrate the sample for 2 min at 22.5°C and analyze by three measurements, each containing 11 runs.
Each run takes 10 s, resulting in a measurement time of approximately 4 min per detergent stock concentration.
Remove the sample solution from the cuvette using a Pasteur pipette.
Add approximately 0.5 mL of the next detergent stock concentration (0.001 mg/mL) to the cuvette.
Remove the solution from the cuvette.
Fit both regions to linear functions.
Take the concentration at the intersection as the cac value.
Measure detergent solutions in order from lowest to highest concentrations.
Obtain diffusion coefficients and hydrodynamic radii using Zetasizer Nano-ZS software.
Store sample solutions at 4°C for up to 12 months if needed.
Solubilize membrane suspensions with detergent.
Purify membrane proteins by immobilized metal affinity chromatography (IMAC).
Elute membrane proteins from IMAC columns.
Quantify eluted membrane proteins by absorption spectroscopy.
Prepare buffer solutions using the hybrid detergent stock solution made in step 4c.
Add the hybrid detergent stock solution to wash, elute, and wash elute buffers to achieve a final concentration of 2× the cac of the detergent (here 420 μM).
Store prepared buffer solutions at 4°C for up to 1 week.
Cool all buffer and detergent solutions on ice before use.
Put 900 μL extraction buffer into a centrifuge tube.
Add 100 μL of hybrid detergent stock solution (10 w%) to the tube.
Add 100 μL of membrane suspension to the tube.
Mix the solution by inverting it.
Cool the samples on ice for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge the samples at 12,000 × g at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Agitate the bottle containing Ni-NTA agarose until homogeneous.
Add 800 μL of the Ni-NTA agarose suspension to empty spin columns.
Remove the bottom caps of the columns.
Apply pressure with your fingertip onto the upper opening of each column to initiate solvent flow.
Add 1 mL detergent-containing wash buffer to the columns and wait for it to run through.
Pass additional detergent-containing wash buffers through the columns: 4 mL wash elute buffer.
Isolate clarified supernatants from step 5f.
Load isolated supernatants onto the spin columns.
Do not apply pressure with your fingertip onto the upper openings of the columns at this step.
Pass the following detergent-containing buffer through every column to elute purified membrane proteins: 400 μL elution buffer.
Collect the flowthrough.
Measure the absorbance values at 485 nm for each sample on a photometer (IMPLEN).
Plot the absorbance values obtained at 485 nm against detergents to compare relative protein yields.
Transfer eluted membrane protein samples to Amicon 0.5 mL centrifugal filters with MWCOs lower than the molecular weight of the investigated complex if necessary.
Concentrate samples by centrifugation (12,000 × g at 4°C for 5 minutes).
Determine concentrated sample volumes using an Eppendorf pipette.
Measure the A485 value with a microvolume photometer (IMPLEN) for diluted samples.
Apply volume correction to absorbance values by dividing obtained sample volume by the largest sample volume and multiplying by the absorbance value at 485 nm.
Plot corrected A485 nm values against detergent abbreviations to compare relative protein yields.
Take 75 μL Zeba™ Spin Desalting columns (MWCO = 7 kDa) and remove lids from bottom and top of the column.
Place the column into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube and remove shipping buffer by centrifugation (1,200 × g at 4°C for 1 min).
Load the column with 50 μL detergent-containing ammonium acetate buffer and centrifuge (1,200 × g at 4°C for 1 min).
Discard the eluted solvent.
Repeat steps three times in total.
Load the column with 8 μL of concentrated protein solution, place the column into a fresh 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube, and centrifuge (1,200 × g at 4°C for 1 min).
Store Eppendorf tubes containing the eluted membrane protein samples on ice.
Dilute membrane protein-detergent mixtures with detergent-containing ammonium acetate to a comparable concentration between 1 – 10 μM.
Load .ipr file into the instrument software Tune.
Load 2 μL of eluted protein solution into a gold-coated nMS capillary.
Place gold-coated nMS capillary into the nMS interface.
Set HCD voltage to 0 V and capillary temperature to 50°C.
Apply gas pressure to the capillary until a small bubble is formed at the front end.
Connect the nMS interface with the MS instrument.
Switch on nMS voltage (capillary voltage).
Acquire mass spectra for approximately 5 seconds and save the data.
Load MS data into the software Xcalibur.
Sum up the acquired mass spectra.
Check if protein signals are visible.
Increase HCD voltage by 50 V steps.
At each HCD voltage change, acquire spectra for 5 seconds.
Check if protein signals are visible after each increase in HCD voltage.
Identify the minimal HCD voltage required to obtain a resolved spectrum of the target protein with no detergents bound.
Continue increasing HCD voltage until reaching a maximum of 300 V.
Assign membrane protein charge states by using MaCSED or Unidec.
Assign signals for membrane protein apo form and membrane protein-lipid complexes.
Compare the analyte mass obtained from MaCSED or Unidec with the theoretical protein mass calculated from its amino acid sequence or the sum of the theoretical protein mass and its ligand complexes.
Compare similar charge states to assess relative trends in membrane protein delipidation.
